comments: Common-sense estimate (Claude, for LCA-team review): Part of the functional unit (3 m partition, standard storey height), must equal for all compared walls. | earlier note: part of the functional unit - keep equal across the compared walls

description: Wall height divided by wall thickness
comments: Common-sense estimate (Claude, for LCA-team review): Height/thickness = 10 gives a 0.30 m wall, the thickness of the RAW printed wall (lci_raw_biopol uses the same 10); a thin unreinforced earth wall is limited by slenderness, so 8-12 (0.25-0.375 m) is realistic. Note: this makes adobe ~2.6x thicker than the clay brick partition (0.115 m), so its mass per m of wall is much higher.

description: Density of the adobe wall (mortar is the same material)
source: common sense: adobe/earth block dry density 1200-1900 kg/m3
comments: Common-sense estimate (Claude, for LCA-team review): Dry adobe with straw/fibre is 1200-1900 kg/m3 (fully compacted soil reaches ~2000+, which adobe usually does not). Typical 1700, range narrowed to 1300-1900 (was 1360-2040). | earlier note: Adobe brick density: no adobe-specific source retrieved (compacted raw earth optimum 2160 kg/m3 is for rammed earth, not adobe). Kept placeholder. | [2026-10-16] Range 1360-2040 -> 1530-1870: adobe ~1500-1900 kg/m3 (+-10 %)

description: Amount of adobe brick per kg of product
comments: Common-sense estimate (Claude, for LCA-team review): Wall = bricks laid in earth mortar of the same material, so 1 kg wall = 1 kg adobe. | [2026-10-16] Fixed (was a +-20 % range): 1 kg of product is 1 kg of this material

description: Years the product lasts in use
comments: Common-sense estimate (Claude, for LCA-team review): Protected interior earth walls last as long as the building if kept dry, but unfired earth is moisture-sensitive and partitions get rebuilt at refurbishments. Set at 60 y (clay brick 75 y): a modest discount for moisture risk, range 40-100. | earlier note: No source found for interior adobe walls. Protected, dry earthen walls can last centuries, so 50 y is conservative and penalises adobe vs clay brick (75 y): decision for you.

description: kg of adobe brick that goes to waste inert landfilling at end of life, per kg of product
source: common sense; adobe is infinitely recyclable in principle (Materials and Structures 2025)
comments: Common-sense estimate (Claude, for LCA-team review): Unfired adobe is not fired ceramic: it can be re-wetted and reformed or used as fill/plaster, so about half is reused, half is disposed as inert waste. Range widened to 25-75% because practice is so uncertain. | earlier note: the other 50 % is reused (no treatment). Recycling of raw earth has no activity on the sheet, so it is not modelled.

description: Country whose electricity mix is displaced by energy recovered at end of life
comments: Common-sense estimate (Claude, for LCA-team review): Model choice, not a measurement: NL because the RAW project and its electricity/heat credit assumptions are Dutch and the ecoinvent NL grid is available. Only matters for the energy credit of incineration; change on study_setup if you model another country.
